title: Police K9 Takes Down Gunman Accused Of Las Vegas Shooting Spree
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
North Las Vegas, Nevada — On September 15, 2025, North Las Vegas Police first discovered a bullet hole inside a lieutenant’s office at their Traffic Division building at 6445 North Palmer St.. At the time, officers had no suspect and little evidence, but over the next several days, the same building was shot at multiple times while staff were inside. Then, the violence spread, bullets struck nearby homes, vehicles, and even a 13-year-old boy who was shot while walking home from school on September 19. His injuries were not life-threatening, but the randomness of the attacks terrified the community and puzzled investigators. Police initially believed the incidents were separate, but as evidence mounted, including ballistic matches, surveillance footage, and GPS data, detectives realized they were all connected and likely committed by the same shooter. 

Officers began surveilling the area near Centennial Parkway and Pecos Road, hoping to catch him in the act. On September 26, 2025, they heard a gunshot during a nearby traffic stop and spotted a silver four-door car speeding away, matching the suspect vehicle from earlier shootings. After a high-speed chase that reached 100 mph, officers cornered 36-year-old Hector Andres Rodriguez, at a gas station. A K9 unit helped bring him down and take him into custody. Police later found two guns, one on him and another at his home, both tied through forensic testing to numerous shootings, including those at Mandalay Bay, the Wynn, and Clark County Family Court. Investigators now believe Rodriguez’s motive was rooted in anti-police sentiment, as he had recorded videos threatening to kill officers before his arrest.
